items.text: For satalite work I really prefer to use two radios. No need for a diplexer and affords more overall flexibility. I use a kenwood D74a for RX where I can record the session and a mobile radio for TX set to medium power where I can drive more watts and punch through the noise. Before I was using the mobile radio I was using my older kenwood F6a for TX.
Oh no, that's sad! I used to hang there 2002-2006 ish. Good times.

Actually of you look at the connector base you will see that this one has a thin rubber band under the knurling. The diamond antenna does not have this but the Maldol Antennas MH-209 does. 

https://www.dxengineering.com/parts/mld-mh-209?seid=dxese1&cm_mmc=pla-google-_-shopping-_-dxese1-_-maldol-antennas&gclid=EAIaIQobChMI1KiX-efK4QIVvh-tBh1jvQjTEAQYAiABEgJLg_D_BwE

Eh. I have the maldol version and the diamond SRH-805. They probably all have equally poor performance, comet also has a similar model, the MH-209. 

The reality is none of these antennas are going to be signifigantly different from each other, they are designed for convenience.

They are great for when you are close range in a group or getting into a local repeter with good coverage in your area. I love them for a compact digital HT setup when using hotspots. 

I would say pick one that fits your HT well and has the native connector for your radio. Beware of knockoffs for all these antennas all over Amazon and eBay though. 

I use a Chinese import antenna on my anytone 868 for local repeaters and hotspots at home that has had surprisingly good performance. I like that it fits snug on my radio and fills out the antenna recess. 

NKTECH NK-761M https://www.amazon.com/dp/B071P7LQ3D/ref=cm_sw_r_cp_api_i_cfoSCb6SBX0PJ

I use one zone per DMR repeater or hotspot. Then one zone per group of analog memories, in the same way I use memory banks in other radios. I don't like to mix digital repeaters in the same zone, otherwise I find it easy to get mixed up since I can often hit 2 or 3 dmr repeaters from the same spot.

Everyone wants to rave about the FT-60 but at this stage of the game I think there are better options for 160 bucks. Afterall it is nearly a 15 year old model complete with segment LCD and nicad battery.

I actually WANT to be a icom fan. I think they have the best fit and finish of the majior 3 vendors. They also have some great technology and usability features. I had a IC-W32A back in the day that was awesome. 

Right now I can't justify a second dstar radio and I didn't like that the ID-51 lacked a keypad or touchscreen. If I were to get a new dual band mobile it would undoubtedly be a IC-5100 and they are killing it with the IC-7300 / IC-9700. I'm also considering picking up a IC-7100.
